name: Unitarian churches

facts.value: Separate communities in Poland and Hungary. English denomination from Lindsey's secession in 1773. American Unitarian Association 1825

citations.locator: Unitarianism (A. Gordon and G. W. Cooke)
citations.excerpt: this type of doctrine ultimately became the badge of separate religious communities, in Poland (extinct), in Hungary (still flourishing), and at a much later date in England.
The formation of a distinct Unitarian denomination dates from the secession (1773) of Theophilus Lindsey (1723-1808) from the Anglican Church
which was emphasized in 1825 by the formation of the American Unitarian Association at Boston.

facts.value_before_verify: 16th century in Poland and Transylvania. English denomination from Lindsey's secession in 1773. American Unitarian Association 1825

facts.value: The Godhead exists in the person of the Father alone. Toleration, few essentials, no formulated creed, and historical study of Scripture.

citations.excerpt: based, as opposed to orthodox Trinitarianism, on the unipersonality of the Godhead, i.e. that the Godhead exists in the person of the Father alone.
namely, a large degree of toleration, a minimizing of essentials, a repugnance to formulated creed, an historical study of Scripture.

facts.value: Anti-Trinitarian churches. The Reformation was attended in every European country by an outbreak of anti-Trinitarian opinion. In Transylvania Francis Dávid became anti-Trinitarian, and in America a division in the Congregational churches led to the American Unitarian Association in 1825.

citations.excerpt: His influence was exerted on Francis Dávid (1510–1579), who was successively Catholic, Lutheran, Calvinist and anti-Trinitarian.
The result was a growing division in the Congregational churches, which was emphasized in 1825 by the formation of the American Unitarian Association at Boston.

citations.locator: Unitarianism (A. Gordon and G. W. Cooke)
citations.excerpt: it is certain that the Reformation of the 16th century was in every European country attended by an outbreak more or less serious of anti-Trinitarian opinion.

facts.value_before_verify: Antitrinitarian churches arising from the Reformation. In Transylvania Francis Dávid led the movement from the 1560s. In America a division in the Congregational churches produced the American Unitarian Association.

research_notes: Multiple national origins; start marked disputed because different countries have different dates. Lane parent g160.
